provenance.notes: Researched definition in tools/extract/patterns/src/apg-2.mjs. Every binding was checked against the APG page; roles and key names are cross-checked mechanically against apg-skeleton.json and aria-roles.json. Arabic name is an unreviewed translation.

attributes.name: aria-labelledby
attributes.values: IDREF of the visible label; otherwise aria-label

attributes.name: aria-selected
attributes.values: true on the active tab, false on the others

keyboard.action: Into the tab list: focus the active tab. From the tab list: move to the next element in the page sequence, which is the tabpanel unless its first meaningful element is focusable.
Move focus to the previous tab, wrapping from first to last; optionally activate it.
Move focus to the next tab, wrapping from last to first; optionally activate it.
Move focus to the next tab, wrapping; optionally activate it. Not handled in a horizontal tab list, so the page can scroll.
Move focus to the previous tab, wrapping; optionally activate it. Not handled in a horizontal tab list.
Activate the focused tab if it was not activated on focus.
Move focus to the first tab; optionally activate it.
Move focus to the last tab; optionally activate it.
If the tab has a popup menu, open it.
If deletion is allowed: close the tab and its panel, focus the following tab (or the preceding one if it was last) and optionally activate it; if no tab remains, focus a logical element elsewhere.

focus.exit: Tab goes to the tabpanel, which has tabindex 0 when it contains no focusable element or its first content element is not focusable.
focus.tabStops: One for the tab list, plus the panel.
focus.note: Automatic activation on focus is recommended when panels show without noticeable delay; otherwise manual activation.

variants: with a popup menu per tab

rtlDecisions.question: In a horizontal roving-focus composite (tabs, toolbar, menubar, radio group, toggle group), which arrow moves to the next item in RTL?
rtlDecisions.apg: Silent, apart from one aside in the tabs page that calls the last tab the right-most "in a left-to-right horizontal tab list". Keys are named physically: Right Arrow is next.

libraries.behaviour: ArrowLeft is next in RTL for tabs, toolbar and horizontal radio groups; vertical arrows never flip.
The composite root swaps the forward and backward horizontal keys when direction is rtl.
The roving focus group swaps ArrowLeft and ArrowRight before mapping a key to a focus intent when dir is rtl; toggle group, tabs, toolbar, radio group and menubar all pass dir through it.
Tabs and ToggleButtonGroup pass isRtl to the roving tabindex root.
Tabs flip the arrow offset when rtl and the tab bar is top or bottom; a horizontal menu maps Left to next when rtl.

rtlDecisions.reason: Items are laid out from inline-start, so the arrow that points at the visually following item must move to it. All five libraries agree.

data.notes: RTL: in a horizontal tab list the first tab is on the right, ArrowLeft goes to the next tab and ArrowRight to the previous; Home and End still mean first and last. React Aria applies the swap in vertical tab lists too (its left/right delegate follows the locale direction regardless of orientation), which only matters if a vertical list listens to horizontal arrows; the page does not bind them there. After Delete in RTL "the following tab" is the one to the left.
